method.wall: time.perf_counter around the named call (in-process) or subprocess (CLI/suite)
method.cold: CLI: first of 5 fresh Python processes. In-process workers: first call in a fresh interpreter (n=3 interpreters). Suite: one wall; not split cold/warm.
method.warm: CLI: remaining 4 processes (page cache / dyld). In-process: 5 subsequent calls in the same interpreter (15 samples across 3 processes).
method.anti_goodhart: A 20% LOC cut that inlines untrusted pytest into Engine is a failure. py_compile became in-process compile(); contained pytest stays a killable session. grok-run dry_run still spawns grok-run so the printed inner command is grok-run's, not a second Python reconstruction.

scope_guard.restored_why: pytest of tools/headless rewrites those receipts; they are not this gate. Restored from git show HEAD:<path> (git restore is blocked by index.lock in this sandbox).

why: GrokBridge._launch already constructs the grok-run argv in Python (handle.command_run). The 425ms is not argv construction; it is Node grok-run starting under GROK_DRYRUN=1.

dry_run's value is that it shows the command grok-run WILL ACTUALLY RUN: the inner `grok` argv (resolved_command) plus a task dir grok-run allocates. That translation lives in grok-run, not this repo.
GrokBridge never invents a task id; it parses grok-run's `task dir:` line. Skipping the spawn would require inventing one.
find_grok_run / shutil.which is 0.051ms median (tool_discovery). Already fast; not optimized.

verifier_dispatch.label: command_is_admissible + Engine._validate (2 .py files + 1 pytest file)
verifier_dispatch.what_changed: Engine._validate uses compile() in-process (kind remains 'py_compile' on the receipt). Engine._pytest_importable uses importlib.util.find_spec('pytest'). Contained pytest is still _run_contained_subprocess (start_new_session + killpg). mutation.validate_python_syntax shares compile_python_file.
verifier_dispatch.command: PYTHONPATH=. python3 -c 'from hcli.engine import Engine; from hcli.events import EventBus; from hcli.verifier_pipeline import command_is_admissible; from hcli.workspace import Workspace; ... engine._validate([calc.py, test_calc.py], ["test_calc.py"])'  # 3 fresh interpreters; first call=cold, next 5=warm
verifier_dispatch.fixture: calc.py `def add`; test_calc.py asserts add(2,3)==5; command_is_admissible('python3 -m pytest test_calc.py -q') then Engine._validate
verifier_dispatch.remaining_cost_is: the contained pytest subprocess (isolation boundary). Warm ≈ cold after the py_compile/import-pytest ceremony is gone, which is the expected shape.
